description: The image displays three pie charts labeled “easy,” “medium,” and “hard,” each illustrating the distribution of four categories—N+K+, N−K+, N−K−, and N+K−—as defined in the legend, with corresponding colors: teal, beige, orange, and red, respectively. In the “easy” chart, N+K+ accounts for 40.6% (teal), N−K+ for 45.9% (beige), N−K− for 10.1% (orange), and N+K− for 3.3% (red). The “medium” chart shows N+K+ at 44.6% (teal), N−K+ at 44.3% (beige), N−K− at 7.2% (orange), and N+K− at 3.9% (red). In the “hard” chart, N+K+ is 20.1% (teal), N−K+ is 36.2% (beige), N−K− is 7.0% (orange), and N+K− is not labeled with a percentage but appears as a small red slice; notably, the orange slice for N−K− is partially obscured by a gray rectangular overlay. All charts are positioned above the label “CoT,” suggesting these distributions relate to Chain-of-Thought reasoning performance across difficulty levels. Percentages are displayed inside each slice, and the slices are arranged in descending order clockwise from the top.
